knowledge-base.overview: Unity 2022 LTS+ guardrails, MonoBehaviour patterns, component architecture, ScriptableObjects, input system, physics, UI, object pooling, and testing for games, VR/AR, and simulations. Loaded automatically when agents work on Unity C# scripts (.cs files with UnityEngine references).

core-principles.principle: One MonoBehaviour = one responsibility. Decompose behavior into small, focused scripts on GameObjects.
Combine components on GameObjects; avoid deep class hierarchies. Use interfaces (IDamageable, IInteractable) for polymorphism.
Use ScriptableObjects for configuration, tuning, and shared data — no singletons for data.
Decouple systems with C# events, UnityEvents, or ScriptableObject event channels. Publishers should not know about subscribers.
Never call Find, GetComponent, or allocate in Update or FixedUpdate — cache in Awake.

guardrail.rule: Never call GameObject.Find, FindObjectOfType, or GetComponent in Update, FixedUpdate, or LateUpdate. Cache all references in Awake or Start.
Never use gameObject.tag == "Tag" for tag comparison. Use CompareTag("Tag") which avoids GC allocation from string creation.
guardrail.bad: if (gameObject.tag == "Enemy") { } // allocates a new string every call

guardrail.rule: Never move a Rigidbody in Update. Physics operations (MovePosition, AddForce, velocity assignment) must happen in FixedUpdate to stay in sync with the physics engine.
Never allocate in hot paths (Update, FixedUpdate, OnCollision*, OnTrigger*). Avoid new List, new string, LINQ, and string concatenation in these methods.
Subscribe to events in OnEnable and unsubscribe in OnDisable. This ensures subscriptions survive enable/disable cycles and prevent callbacks on disabled components.
Use [SerializeField] private instead of public for inspector-accessible fields. Keep the public API minimal.
guardrail.bad: public float moveSpeed = 5f; // exposed unnecessarily to other scripts

guardrail.rule: Apply [RequireComponent(typeof(T))] when a script depends on another component. This prevents misconfiguration in the Inspector and forces the component to be present.
Use Time.deltaTime for frame-independent movement in Update. Use Time.fixedDeltaTime in FixedUpdate (it is constant but explicit use is good documentation).
Use TextMeshPro for all text rendering. Never use legacy UI.Text — it has worse performance and no rich text support.
Pool frequently-spawned objects (bullets, particles, enemies, VFX). Never call Instantiate/Destroy in tight loops or per-frame logic.
Use the new Input System package. Never use legacy Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.*) in new code. Define actions in .inputactions asset files.
Use Addressables for runtime asset loading. Minimize Resources/ folder content — Resources.Load() keeps assets in memory and increases build size.

project-structure.description: Feature-grouped Assets layout with _Project/ prefix to sort above Unity built-in folders.
project-structure.example: MyGame/ ├── Assets/ │ ├── _Project/ │ │ ├── Art/ # Materials, Models, Sprites, Textures │ │ ├── Audio/ # Music, SFX AudioClips │ │ ├── Prefabs/ │ │ │ ├── Characters/ │ │ │ ├── Environment/ │ │ │ └── UI/ │ │ ├── Scenes/ # MainMenu.unity, Level01.unity, etc. │ │ ├── Scripts/ │ │ │ ├── Core/ # GameManager, SceneLoader, ServiceLocator │ │ │ ├── Player/ # PlayerController, PlayerHealth, PlayerInput │ │ │ ├── Enemies/ # AI, spawning, enemy type scripts │ │ │ ├── UI/ # HUDController, MenuController │ │ │ ├── Systems/ # AudioManager, SaveSystem, ObjectPool │ │ │ └── Data/ # ScriptableObject definitions, structs │ │ ├── ScriptableObjects/ # ItemData, EnemyConfig, GameSettings assets │ │ └── Settings/ # InputActions.inputactions │ ├── Plugins/ │ └── Resources/ # Keep minimal — prefer Addressables ├── Packages/manifest.json ├── ProjectSettings/ ├── Tests/ │ ├── EditMode/ # Pure logic tests (no MonoBehaviour) │ └── PlayMode/ # Component behavior tests (lifecycle) └── .gitignore

notes.note: Group assets by feature (Player/) not by type (Scripts/) for maintainability
Editor/ folders for editor-only scripts (excluded from runtime builds)
ScriptableObjects/ for runtime configuration assets visible in Inspector

lifecycle.description: MonoBehaviour execution order. Understanding this is critical for correct initialization.

rules.rule: Awake: initialize self-references (GetComponent). Never access other objects here — they may not be initialized.
Start: access other objects. All Awake() calls are complete.
OnEnable/OnDisable: always pair — subscribe and unsubscribe events here.
FixedUpdate: all Rigidbody operations; runs at fixed physics timestep, not per frame.

pattern.name: Singleton Manager (DontDestroyOnLoad)
pattern.description: Use sparingly. Prefer ServiceLocator for testability. Protect against duplicate instances.

pattern.name: Health Component (Interface + UnityEvent)
pattern.description: Implement IDamageable interface. Use UnityEvents so designers can wire callbacks in Inspector without code.

pattern.name: Player Controller (New Input System)
pattern.description: RequireComponent on dependencies. Cache in Awake. Wire input in OnEnable/OnDisable.

scriptable-objects.description: Use ScriptableObjects for item definitions, enemy configs, game settings, and event channels. They live as .asset files, are editable in the Inspector, and shared across scenes.

object-pooling.description: Pool anything spawned frequently. Never Instantiate/Destroy in per-frame or per-collision code.

testing.stack: NUnit (Unity Test Runner), EditMode (pure logic), PlayMode (MonoBehaviour lifecycle)

rules.rule: Edit Mode tests for pure data structures and logic with no MonoBehaviour dependency
Play Mode tests for component behavior requiring Awake/Start/Update lifecycle
Always Destroy test GameObjects in TearDown or inline after assertions
Use [UnityTest] with IEnumerator and yield return null to advance one frame in Play Mode tests

commands.cmd: Use Roslyn analyzers in Unity 2022+ via NuGet or included packages

quick-reference.item: GetComponent / Find in Awake only; never in Update, FixedUpdate, or callbacks
Rigidbody operations in FixedUpdate; Time.deltaTime in Update; Time.fixedDeltaTime in FixedUpdate
Subscribe OnEnable, unsubscribe OnDisable — always paired
Use [SerializeField] private; group with [Header("Section")]; [RequireComponent] for hard dependencies
No new collections, no LINQ, no string concat in Update/FixedUpdate; reuse with .Clear()
New Input System + .inputactions asset; wire in OnEnable/OnDisable
Pool bullets, particles, enemies; ObjectPool<T> with Get/Return methods
ScriptableObjects for config, event channels, item definitions — shareable across scenes
EditMode for pure logic; PlayMode with [UnityTest] + yield return null for lifecycle tests
